pointers.sentence: So a backend writes the methods that touch its store ([The cache backends](cache-backends.md)), and `BaseCache` does what is the same for all (`django/core/cache/backends/base.py:BaseCache`).

`CacheHandler.create_connection` copies the alias's dictionary, pops `"BACKEND"` and `"LOCATION"`, the location defaulting to the empty string, imports the class and calls it with the location and the rest of the dictionary (`django/core/cache/__init__.py:CacheHandler.create_connection`).

A class that will not import, and an alias `CACHES` lacks, are refused with `InvalidCacheBackendError`, the second as `CacheHandler.exception_class` (`django/utils/connection.py:BaseConnectionHandler.__getitem__`).

The handler leaves `BaseConnectionHandler.thread_critical` false, where the database's handler sets it, so its asgiref `Local` is a context variable (`asgiref:asgiref/local.py:Local`): each thread still makes its own backends, but code run through `sync_to_async` or `async_to_sync` sees its caller's.

`cache` is a `ConnectionProxy` of the handler and `DEFAULT_CACHE_ALIAS`: each read of an attribute the proxy lacks, each attribute set or deleted on it, and `in` and `==`, go to `caches["default"]`, looked up again each time (`django/utils/connection.py:ConnectionProxy`).
`close_caches`, a receiver of `request_finished`, closes the backends the current thread or context has made (`django/core/cache/__init__.py:close_caches`).
`BaseCache.__init__` reads the rest of the dictionary (`django/core/cache/backends/base.py:BaseCache.__init__`):

`BaseCache.make_key` passes the key, the prefix and a version, the call's or else the cache's, to the key function, and `default_key_func` joins the three with colons (`django/core/cache/backends/base.py:BaseCache.make_key`).
In Django's documentation, a prefix keeps apart the Django instances that share one cache, and a version retires old values without clearing the rest (`docs/topics/cache.txt`).
`get_key_func` uses a callable `"KEY_FUNCTION"` as it is and imports a dotted path (`django/core/cache/backends/base.py:get_key_func`).

`BaseCache.validate_key` issues a `CacheKeyWarning` for each message of `memcache_key_warnings`: a key longer than `MEMCACHE_MAX_KEY_LENGTH`, 250, or holding a control character or a space (`django/core/cache/backends/base.py:memcache_key_warnings`).

`BaseCache.get_backend_timeout` makes the sentinel the cache's default, keeps `None`, and adds a number of seconds to `time.time()`, giving the moment of expiry (`django/core/cache/backends/base.py:BaseCache.get_backend_timeout`).

Their docstrings fix their returns: `add`, whether it stored the value, which it does only for an absent key; `touch`, whether the key was there; `delete`, whether it succeeded (`django/core/cache/backends/base.py:BaseCache.add`).
`BaseCache.__contains__` calls `has_key`, its comment says, so that `in` follows any override of it (`django/core/cache/backends/base.py:BaseCache.__contains__`).
`BaseCache.get_or_set` gets the key; on a miss it calls the default if callable, `add`s the result and gets the key again (`django/core/cache/backends/base.py:BaseCache.get_or_set`).

`BaseCache.incr_version` gets the value at a version, the cache's by default, sets it at the version plus the delta, deletes the old entry and returns the new version (`django/core/cache/backends/base.py:BaseCache.incr_version`).

A key set for ten seconds and incremented had 300 left on `FileBasedCache`, which inherits the base's `incr`, and ten on `LocMemCache`, whose own leaves the expiry alone (`django/core/cache/backends/locmem.py:LocMemCache.incr`).

Each method of the API, but `in` and the helpers for keys and timeouts, has a twin with an `a` in front, such as `BaseCache.aget`, and every twin is `BaseCache`'s: no backend Django ships writes one, and its documentation says Django does not yet support asynchronous caching (`docs/topics/cache.txt`).

The twins of the methods a backend must write, and `BaseCache.aclose`, call the method through `sync_to_async` with `thread_sensitive=True`, on the thread kept for such work, under ASGI the request's own ([Sync and async in one chain](../handlers/async.md)) (`django/core/cache/backends/base.py:BaseCache.aget`).

The twins of the defaults, but for `BaseCache.adecr` and `BaseCache.adecr_version`, which call `aincr` and `aincr_version`, run the backend's replacement, if it has one, in one such call, and otherwise repeat the default's steps through the other twins, each a crossing of its own (`django/core/cache/backends/base.py:BaseCache.aget_or_set`).
